So you would get an email from the sales person at the bank who has just closed the deal and is now selling these (this bank is the broker/dealer who bought it?) There's not really much of a secondary market - the initial investors would often hold on to these. There is something around Bloomberg - you can go there and see what's available, if someone has a number of notes from a iven tranche, that they are willing to sell. So there's no transpoarency (!!) Sales would be OTC but less transparent e.g. if you look up a normal OTC stock, you would be able to see more of this information, than in these (non Agency) MBS issues and other SF. classes.label: standardized futures listing terms
classes.definition: contract terms established by a derivatives exchange that apply to any listing of a futures contract on that exchange.

classes.name: standardized futures terms
classes.label: standardized futures terms
classes.definition: contract terms established by a derivatives exchange that apply to any futures contract traded on that exchange

classes.name: basket option
classes.label: basket option
classes.definition: option whose underlying asset is a group, or basket, of commodities, securities, indices, or currencies

classes.name: bond option
classes.label: bond option
classes.definition: option giving the buyer (holder) the right, but not the obligation, to buy or sell (depending on whether it is a call or a put) a bond at a certain price on or before a specified date

classes.name: butterfly
classes.label: butterfly
classes.definition: strategy that combines bull and bear spreads with a fixed risk and capped profit

classes.name: call option
classes.label: call option
classes.definition: option giving the buyer (holder) the right, but not the obligation, to buy the assets specified at a fixed price or formula, on or before a specified date

classes.name: capped option
classes.label: capped option
classes.definition: option with an established profit cap or cap price

classes.name: collar
classes.label: collar
classes.definition: option trading strategy that involves buying a downside put and selling an upside call that is implemented to protect against large losses, but which also limits large upside gains

classes.name: condor spread
classes.label: condor spread
classes.definition: non-directional options strategy that limits both gains and losses while seeking to profit from either low or high volatility

classes.name: covered call
classes.label: covered call
classes.definition: call option in which the seller (investor) owns an equivalent amount of the underlying security

classes.name: equity option
classes.label: equity option
classes.definition: option giving the buyer (holder) the right, but not the obligation, to buy (via a call option) or sell (via a put option) the underlying equity assets specified at a pre-determined price (i.e., the strike price, fixed or calculated), on or before a specified date (the expiration date)

classes.name: exotic option
classes.label: exotic option
classes.definition: option that has a non-standard payout structure or other feature

classes.name: extrinsic value
classes.label: extrinsic value
classes.definition: measure of the difference between the market price of an option, called the premium, and its intrinsic value

classes.name: fence
classes.label: fence
classes.definition: option trading strategy that uses options to limit the range of possible returns on a financial instrument

classes.name: fixed income option
classes.label: fixed income option
classes.definition: option giving the buyer (holder) the right, but not the obligation, to buy (via a call option) or sell (via a put option) the underlying fixed income assets specified at a pre-determined price (i.e., the strike price, fixed or calculated), on or before a specified date (the expiration date)

classes.name: interest rate option
classes.label: interest rate option
classes.definition: option that giving the buyer (holder) the right, but not the obligation, to receive a cash payment if market interest rate of a reference rate is higher or lower, depending on the option, than the strike rate of the option

classes.name: intrinsic value
classes.label: intrinsic value
classes.definition: measure of what an asset is worth, i.e. with respect to its current price

classes.name: iron butterfly
classes.label: iron butterfly
classes.definition: butterfly strategy that consists of two call options and two put options, three strike prices and the same expiration date

classes.name: iron condor
classes.label: iron condor
classes.definition: condor strategy consisting of two puts (one long and one short) and two calls (one long and one short), and four strike prices, all with the same expiration date

classes.name: long-term equity anticipation security
classes.label: long-term equity anticipation security
classes.definition: equity option that allows the holder to buy or sell shares of stock with expiration dates that are longer than one year, and typically up to three years from issue

classes.name: moneyness
classes.label: moneyness
classes.definition: classifier for a derivative relating its strike price to the price of its underlying asset

classes.name: option holder
classes.label: option holder
classes.definition: party that owns an option

classes.name: option issuer
classes.label: option issuer
classes.definition: issuer granting the rights defined in the option in exchange for some consideration

classes.name: option on future
classes.label: option on future
classes.definition: option that gives the holder the right, but not the obligation, to buy or sell a specific futures contract at a specified price on or before the option's expiration date

classes.name: option premium
classes.label: option premium
classes.definition: current market price of an option contract

classes.name: option premium formula
classes.label: option premium formula
classes.definition: expression used to calculate the premium based either on the price per option or percentage of the notional amount

classes.name: option trading strategy
classes.label: option trading strategy
classes.definition: trading tactic involving more than one option type, strike price, or expiration date on the same underlying asset

classes.name: protective collar
classes.label: protective collar
classes.definition: collar that consists of a covered call and protective put

classes.name: protective put
classes.label: protective put
classes.definition: put option giving the buyer (holder) the right, but not the obligation, to sell the assets specified at with a strike price equal or close to the current price of the underlying asset, on or before a specified date

classes.name: put option
classes.label: put option
classes.definition: option giving the buyer (holder) the right, but not the obligation, to sell the assets specified at a fixed price or formula, on or before a specified date

classes.name: risk reversal
classes.label: risk reversal
classes.definition: option trading strategy that consists of being short (selling) an out of the money put and being long (i.e., buying) an out of the money call, both with the same maturity

classes.name: standardized options terms
classes.label: standardized options terms
classes.definition: standardized contract terms established by a securities or options exchange or by an options clearing entity

classes.name: straddle
classes.label: straddle
classes.definition: neutral option trading strategy that involves simultaneously buying both a put option and a call option for the underlying security with the same strike price and the same expiration date

classes.name: strangle
classes.label: strangle
classes.definition: option trading strategy in which the investor holds a position in both a call and a put option with different strike prices, but with the same expiration date and underlying asset

classes.name: strike price
classes.label: strike price
classes.definition: price at which a lot of the underlying asset may be bought or sold when the contract is exercised

classes.name: strip strategy
classes.label: strip strategy
classes.definition: option trading strategy that involves a sequential set of options with periodic reset dates, such that each period between resets behaves like an individual option

classes.name: vanilla option
classes.label: vanilla option
classes.definition: common option giving the buyer (holder) the right, but not the obligation, to buy (via a call option) or sell (via a put option) the underlying assets specified at a pre-determined price (i.e., the strike price, fixed or calculated), on or before a specified date (the expiration date)

classes.name: allotment right
classes.label: allotment right
classes.definition: privileges allotted to existing security holders, entitling them to receive new securities free of charge

classes.name: allotment right formula
classes.label: allotment right formula
classes.definition: rule applied to calculate the number of securities for an allotment right, typically based on the number of these instruments that the holder holds

classes.name: barrier instrument-based mini-future certificate
classes.label: barrier instrument-based mini-future certificate
classes.definition: mini-future certificate that immediately expires if the barrier instrument trading price level is breached during product lifetime

classes.name: barrier underlying mini-future certificate
classes.label: barrier underlying mini-future certificate
classes.definition: mini-future certificate that immediately expires if the barrier underlying level is breached during product lifetime

classes.name: basket warrant
classes.label: basket warrant
classes.definition: warrant that permits the holder to acquire a package or group of assets at a specified price during a specified period

classes.name: bond purchase right
classes.label: bond purchase right
classes.definition: purchase right that gives a prospective acquiree's bondholders the right to buy bonds of the firm or bonds of anyone who acquires the firm at a deep discount to their fair market value

classes.name: bond subscription right
classes.label: bond subscription right
classes.definition: subscription right entitling existing bond holders to subscribe to new securities at a price normally lower than the prevailing market price

classes.name: call put warrant
classes.label: call put warrant
classes.definition: warrant that either does not specify call or put features, or that explicitly includes both a call and put feature

classes.name: call warrant
classes.label: call warrant
classes.definition: warrant giving the buyer (holder) the right, but not the obligation, to acquire specific underlying assets during a specified period at a specified price

classes.name: combined instruments purchase right
classes.label: combined instruments purchase right
classes.definition: purchase right that gives a prospective acquiree's holders of multiple securities the right to buy securities of the firm or securities of anyone who acquires the firm at a deep discount to their fair market value

classes.name: combined instruments subscription right
classes.label: combined instruments subscription right
classes.definition: subscription right entitling existing holders of multiple securities to subscribe to new securities at a price normally lower than the prevailing market price

classes.name: commodity warrant
classes.label: commodity warrant
classes.definition: warrant that permits the holder to acquire a specified amount of a commodity during a specified period at a specified price

classes.name: common convertible share purchase right
classes.label: common convertible share purchase right
classes.definition: purchase right that gives a prospective acquiree's common, convertible shareholders the right to buy common, convertible shares of the firm or common, convertible shares of anyone who acquires the firm at a deep discount to their fair market value

classes.name: common convertible share subscription right
classes.label: common convertible share subscription right
classes.definition: subscription right entitling existing common convertible shareholders to subscribe to new securities at a price normally lower than the prevailing market price

classes.name: common share purchase right
classes.label: common share purchase right
classes.definition: purchase right that gives a prospective acquiree's common shareholders the right to buy common shares of the firm or common shares of anyone who acquires the firm at a deep discount to their fair market value

classes.name: common share subscription right
classes.label: common share subscription right
classes.definition: subscription right entitling existing common shareholders to subscribe to new securities at a price normally lower than the prevailing market price

classes.name: constant leverage certificate
classes.label: constant leverage certificate
classes.definition: entitlement that combines the structure of an open-end certificate with a leverage option with no fixed term, making leverage available without a term restriction, without a knock-out barrier dependency

classes.name: covered warrant
classes.label: covered warrant
classes.definition: warrant that gives the holder the right, but not the obligation, to buy (call warrant) or to sell (put warrant) an underlying asset at a specified price (the strike or exercise price) by a predetermined date, issued without an accompanying security by a third party that holds as many securities as would be required if all the warrants are exercised

classes.name: currency warrant
classes.label: currency warrant
classes.definition: warrant that permits the holder to acquire a specified amount in a certain currency at a specified exchange rate during a specified period

classes.name: debt warrant
classes.label: debt warrant
classes.definition: warrant that permits the holder to acquire a specified amount of a debt instrument or related debt observable a specified period at a specified price

classes.name: equity warrant
classes.label: equity warrant
classes.definition: warrant that permits the holder to acquire a specified amount of an equity instrument during a specified period at a specified price

classes.name: exchange-traded warrant
classes.label: exchange-traded warrant
classes.definition: warrant that is listed on a securities exchange

classes.name: exotic warrant
classes.label: exotic warrant
classes.definition: warrant that gives the holder the right (but not the obligation) to buy (or sometimes sell) an underlying asset under non-standard or complex conditions, often involving additional features not found in a plain vanilla (standard) warrant

classes.name: index warrant
classes.label: index warrant
classes.definition: warrant that permits the holder to acquire a specified amount based on the performance of an index during a specified period at a specified price

classes.name: long mini-future certificate
classes.label: long mini-future certificate
classes.definition: mini-future certificate that typically entitles the holder to acquire specific underlying assets during a specified period at a specified price

classes.name: mini-future certificate
classes.label: mini-future certificate
classes.definition: entitlement that combines the structure of an open-end certificate with a leverage option with no fixed term, making leverage available without a term restriction, and whose payoff depends on whether or not the underlying asset has reached or exceeded a predetermined price

classes.name: naked warrant
classes.label: naked warrant
classes.definition: warrant that gives the holder the right, but not the obligation, to buy (call warrant) or to sell (put warrant) an underlying asset at a specified price (the strike or exercise price) by a predetermined date, issued without an accompanying security by a third party that does not hold as many securities as would be required if all the warrants are exercised

classes.name: perpetual warrant
classes.label: perpetual warrant
classes.definition: warrant without an expiration date, giving the holder the right, but not the obligation, to buy (call warrant) or to sell (put warrant) an underlying asset at a certain strike price

classes.name: preferred convertible share purchase right
classes.label: preferred convertible share purchase right
classes.definition: purchase right that gives a prospective acquiree's preferred, convertible shareholders the right to buy preferred, convertible shares of the firm or preferred, convertible shares of anyone who acquires the firm at a deep discount to their fair market value

classes.name: preferred convertible share subscription right
classes.label: preferred convertible share subscription right
classes.definition: subscription right entitling existing preferred, convertible shareholders to subscribe to new securities at a price normally lower than the prevailing market price

classes.name: preferred share purchase right
classes.label: preferred share purchase right
classes.definition: purchase right that gives a prospective acquiree's preferred shareholders the right to buy preferred shares of the firm or preferred shares of anyone who acquires the firm at a deep discount to their fair market value

classes.name: preferred share subscription right
classes.label: preferred share subscription right
classes.definition: subscription right entitling existing preferred shareholders to subscribe to new securities at a price normally lower than the prevailing market price

classes.name: private warrant
classes.label: private warrant
classes.definition: warrant that is not tradable

classes.name: public warrant
classes.label: public warrant
classes.definition: warrant that may be traded over the counter (OTC) or through an exchange

classes.name: purchase right
classes.label: purchase right
classes.definition: anti-takeover device that gives a prospective acquiree's shareholders the right to buy shares of the firm or shares of anyone who acquires the firm at a deep discount to their fair market value

classes.name: put warrant
classes.label: put warrant
classes.definition: warrant giving the buyer (holder) the right, but not the obligation, to sell the assets specified (i.e., acquire cash in exchange for the underlying assets, such as stock) back to the issuer at a fixed price or formula, on or before a specified date

classes.name: short mini-future certificate
classes.label: short mini-future certificate
classes.definition: mini-future certificate that entitles the holder to acquire cash in exchange for specific underlying assets

classes.name: structured warrant
classes.label: structured warrant
classes.definition: warrant that is listed on an exchange, offering investors a way to participate in the price performance of an underlying asset without buying it directly

classes.name: subscription right
classes.label: subscription right
classes.definition: privileges allotted to existing security holders, entitling them to subscribe to new securities at a price normally lower than the prevailing market price

classes.name: traditional warrant
classes.label: traditional warrant
classes.definition: warrant that gives the holder the right, but not the obligation, to buy (call warrant) or to sell (put warrant) an underlying asset at a specified price (the strike or exercise price) by a predetermined date, issued by the issuer of the underlying instrument

classes.name: warrant
classes.label: warrant
classes.definition: entitlement that permits the holder to purchase a specified amount of a financial instrument, commodity, currency or other asset during a specified period at a specified price

classes.name: barrier capital protection certificate
classes.label: barrier capital protection certificate
classes.definition: capital-protected product whose protection is defined as a percentage of the nominal price (e.g. 100 percent), with minimum redemption at expiry equivalent to the capital protection

classes.name: barrier discount certificate
classes.label: barrier discount certificate
classes.definition: participation certificate that enables the investor to acquire the underlying asset at a lower price in return for a limited payout, and for which the maximum redemption amount (Cap) is paid out if the barrier is never breached

classes.name: barrier reverse convertible certificate
classes.label: barrier reverse convertible certificate
classes.definition: participation certificate whose payout is conditional: should the barrier never be breached, the nominal price plus coupon is paid at redemption; if the barrier is breached the product changes into a reverse convertible

classes.name: basket certificate
classes.label: basket certificate
classes.definition: certificate whose underlying asset represents a fraction of a basket of securities that corresponds to the subscription ratio

classes.name: bonus certificate
classes.label: bonus certificate
classes.definition: certificate whose minimum redemption is equal to the nominal value provided the barrier has not been breached, with a greater risk in relation to multiple underlying asset(s) (worst-of), allowing for a higher bonus level or lower barrier, and with a reduced risk compared to a direct investment into the underlying asset(s)

classes.name: capital-protected product
classes.label: capital-protected product
classes.definition: structured product that participates in the performance of a financial asset, such as a stock, fund or index, while protecting the investor's capital

classes.name: capital protection certificate with coupons
classes.label: capital protection certificate with coupons
classes.definition: capital-protected product whose protection is defined as a percentage of the nominal price (e.g. 100 percent), with minimum redemption at expiry equivalent to the capital protection

classes.name: capital protection certificate with participation
classes.label: capital protection certificate with participation
classes.definition: capital-protected product whose protection is defined as a percentage of the nominal amount (e.g. 100 percent), with minimum redemption at expiry equivalent to the capital protection

classes.name: capital protection convertible certificate
classes.label: capital protection convertible certificate
classes.definition: capital-protected product whose protection is defined as a percentage of the nominal price (e.g. 100 percent), with minimum redemption at expiry equivalent to the capital protection

classes.name: discount certificate
classes.label: discount certificate
classes.definition: participation certificate that enables the investor to acquire the underlying asset at a lower price in return for a limited payout, and for which the underlying asset(s) and/or a cash amount is redeemed should the underlying asset close below the strike on expiry, for which, in return, the potential profit is capped

classes.name: express certificate
classes.label: express certificate
classes.definition: participation certificate whose payout is conditional: should the underlying trade above the strike on the observation date, an early redemption consisting of nominal price plus an additional coupon amount is paid

classes.name: index certificate
classes.label: index certificate
classes.definition: certificate whose underlying asset is an index

classes.name: leveraged product
classes.label: leveraged product
classes.definition: structured product that provides a further enhanced yield (over and above that of a yield-enhancement product), often without any limit to the upside participation, and frequently with a stop-loss in order to limit potential capital losses

classes.name: outperformance bonus certificate
classes.label: outperformance bonus certificate
classes.definition: certificate that allows disproportionate participation (outperformance) in positive performance above the strike, in which the minimum redemption is equal to the nominal value provided the barrier has not been breached, with greater risk multiple underlying asset(s) (worst-of) allow for a higher bonus level or lower barrier, and reduced risk compared to a direct investment into the underlying asset(s)

classes.name: outperformance certificate
classes.label: outperformance certificate
classes.definition: certificate that allows disproportionate participation (outperformance) in positive performance above the strike, reflecting underlying price moves 1:1 (adjusted by the conversion ratio and any related fees), and whose risk is comparable to direct investment in the underlying asset(s)

classes.name: participation certificate
classes.label: participation certificate
classes.definition: participation product that provides the possibility to participate in the gains or losses in the price of an asset, subject to counterparty risk

classes.name: participation instrument
classes.label: participation instrument
classes.definition: structured product that provides the possibility to participate in the performance of an asset or basket of assets

classes.name: reverse convertible certificate
classes.label: reverse convertible certificate
classes.definition: participation certificate whose payout is conditional: should the underlying asset close below the strike on expiry, the underlying asset(s) and/ or a cash amount is redeemed; should the underlying asset close above the strike at expiry, the nominal amount plus the coupon is paid at redemption

classes.name: structured product
classes.label: structured product
classes.definition: security whose cash flow characteristics depend upon one or more indices or that have embedded forwards or options or securities where an investor's investment return and the issuer's payment obligations are contingent on, or highly sensitive to, changes in the value of underlying assets, indices, interest rates or cash flows

classes.name: tracker certificate
classes.label: tracker certificate
classes.definition: certificate that reflects underlying price moves 1:1 (adjusted by conversion ratio and any related fees), in which the associated risk is comparable to direct investment in the underlying asset(s)

classes.name: turbo certificate
classes.label: turbo certificate
classes.definition: certificate that acts as a leveraged security, whose price tracks an underlying financial asset's price one for one, and that can be used to go long or short

classes.name: twin-win certificate
classes.label: twin-win certificate
classes.definition: certificate that makes profits possible with rising and falling underlying asset values, in which a falling underlying asset price converts into profit up to the barrier, and whose minimum redemption is equal to the nominal value provided the barrier has not been breached

classes.name: yield-enhancement product
classes.label: yield-enhancement product
classes.definition: structured product that provides a predefined yield in return for a downside risk

classes.name: basis swap
classes.label: basis swap
classes.definition: swap in which payment streams are referenced to different bases

classes.name: correlation leg
classes.label: correlation leg
classes.definition: floating leg of a correlation swap that pays an amount based on the observed average correlation of the prices of a collection of underlying products

classes.name: correlation swap
classes.label: correlation swap
classes.definition: over-the-counter statistical derivative that allows one to hedge risks associated with the observed average correlation of a collection of underlying products

classes.name: dispersion leg
classes.label: dispersion leg
classes.definition: floating leg of a dispersion swap that pays an amount based on the realized dispersion of the price changes of the underlying product

classes.name: dispersion swap
classes.label: dispersion swap
classes.definition: statistical derivative used to hedge on the magnitude of a price movement of an underlying asset

classes.name: excess return swap
classes.label: excess return swap
classes.definition: return swap in which the change in the level of the index will be equal to the returns generated primarily by the changes in price of each of the contracts that comprise the index

classes.name: fixed leg
classes.label: fixed leg
classes.definition: swap leg whose paying party is obligated to make payments from time to time over the term of a swap calculated by reference to a fixed annual rate or consisting of at least one payment of a fixed amount

classes.name: fixed payment leg
classes.label: fixed payment leg
classes.definition: swap leg that specifies contractual terms associated with a schedule of payments for any swap calculated by reference to a fixed annual rate

classes.name: floating leg
classes.label: floating leg
classes.definition: swap leg whose paying party is obligated to make payments from time to time over the term of a swap calculated by reference to some variable rate, calculated based on the change in value of some underlying asset, or consisting of at least one payment of some floating amount

classes.name: index return swap
classes.label: index return swap
classes.definition: return swap in which payments are based on a fee paid to the seller of the swap and on a floating reference price based on changes in the level of an index from an initial level to a level observed on some valuation date(s)

classes.name: major swap participant
classes.label: major swap participant
classes.definition: financial service provider that maintains a substantial position in swaps for any of the major swap categories

classes.name: performance-based variable leg
classes.label: performance-based variable leg
classes.definition: floating leg of a swap that depends on some statistical measure of the performance of the underlier

classes.name: rate-based leg
classes.label: rate-based leg
classes.definition: swap leg of a rate-based swap based on a floating interest, floating inflation or fixed interest rate

classes.name: rates swap
classes.label: rates swap
classes.definition: swap in two counterparties each agree to pay the other cash flows on defined dates during an agreed period, based on a specified notional amount and a floating interest, floating inflation or fixed interest rate

classes.name: realized variable leg
classes.label: realized variable leg
classes.definition: performance-based leg wherein the payment is netted at maturity rather than periodically

classes.name: return leg
classes.label: return leg
classes.definition: leg of a swap in which the income generated by some underlier is paid

classes.name: return swap
classes.label: return swap
classes.definition: swap in which one leg, the return leg, is based on income generated from some underlier

classes.name: simple return leg
classes.label: simple return leg
classes.definition: return leg based strictly on the income generated by the underlying asset, excluding appreciation, decrease in value, capital gains, and fees on any increase in value

classes.name: statistical swap
classes.label: statistical swap
classes.definition: swap that depends on some statistical measure of the performance of the underlier

classes.name: strike leg
classes.label: strike leg
classes.definition: swap leg that specifies a fixed amount, 'the strike', quoted at the time of execution

classes.name: swap
classes.label: swap
classes.definition: derivative instrument whereby counterparties agree to exchange periodic streams of cash flows or liabilities from two different financial instruments with each other

classes.name: swap confirmation
classes.label: swap confirmation
classes.definition: formal confirmation that codifies the terms and conditions specific to a lifecycle event with respect to the overall transaction between the parties

classes.name: swap data repository
classes.label: swap data repository
classes.definition: financial service provider that provides a central facility for swap data reporting and recordkeeping

classes.name: swap dealer
classes.label: swap dealer
classes.definition: non-depository institution such as one that deals in swaps, makes a market in swaps, regularly enters into swaps with counterparties as an ordinary course of business for its own account, and engages in any activity causing the person to be commonly known in the trade as a dealer/market maker in swaps

classes.name: swap leg
classes.label: swap leg
classes.definition: terms defining and the commitment to fulfill cashflow requirements (e.g., interest payments, coupon payments, etc.) for a component of a swap

classes.name: swap leg event
classes.label: swap leg event
classes.definition: swap lifecycle event, such as a payment or rate reset event, that applies to one leg of a swap

classes.name: swap lifecycle event
classes.label: swap lifecycle event
classes.definition: event that occurs during the lifecycle of a swap, where the overall set of events includes those specific to the issuer, front office, middle office, and/or back office processes

classes.name: swap lifecycle event identifier
classes.label: swap lifecycle event identifier
classes.definition: identifier that uniquely identifies a specific event in the lifecycle of a swap

classes.name: swap party
classes.label: swap party
classes.definition: party to a swap and therefore a legal party to the contract that embodies that transaction

classes.name: swap paying party
classes.label: swap paying party
classes.definition: swap party responsible for making payments for a given leg of the transaction as defined in the contract

classes.name: swap receiving party
classes.label: swap receiving party
classes.definition: swap party that receives payments for a given leg of the transaction as defined in the contract

classes.name: swap terms
classes.label: swap terms
classes.definition: legal contractual terms of a swap transaction

classes.name: total return leg
classes.label: total return leg
classes.definition: return leg based on the income generated by the underlying asset as well as any appreciation, decrease in value, capital gains, and fees on any increase in value

classes.name: total return swap
classes.label: total return swap
classes.definition: return swap where the seller agrees to pay the other party the difference in value of some underlying asset multiplied by an agreed-upon notional value should the asset value increase between specified periods of time

classes.name: unique swap identifier
classes.label: unique swap identifier
classes.definition: identifier for a swap that is used in recordkeeping and swap data reporting

classes.name: cross-currency interest rate swap
classes.label: cross-currency interest rate swap
classes.definition: interest rate swap in which the two streams of interest payments are in different currencies

classes.name: fixed fixed interest rate swap
classes.label: fixed fixed interest rate swap
classes.definition: interest rate swap in which both parties pay a fixed interest rate that they could not otherwise obtain outside of a swap arrangement

classes.name: fixed float cross-currency interest rate swap
classes.label: fixed float cross-currency interest rate swap
classes.definition: interest rate swap in which fixed interest payments on the notional are exchanged for floating interest payments and the two streams of interest payments are in different currencies

classes.name: fixed float interest rate swap
classes.label: fixed float interest rate swap
classes.definition: interest rate swap in which fixed interest payments on the notional are exchanged for floating interest payments

classes.name: fixed float single currency interest rate swap
classes.label: fixed float single currency interest rate swap
classes.definition: interest rate swap in which fixed interest payments on the notional are exchanged for floating interest payments and where both payment streams are expressed in terms of the same currency

classes.name: fixed interest rate leg
classes.label: fixed interest rate leg
classes.definition: fixed leg that specifies fixed interest amounts and terms for the payment of that interest

classes.name: float float cross-currency interest rate swap
classes.label: float float cross-currency interest rate swap
classes.definition: interest rate swap that exchanges cashflows based on two different interest rates in different currencies

classes.name: float float interest rate swap
classes.label: float float interest rate swap
classes.definition: interest rate swap that exchanges cashflows based on two different floating interest rates

classes.name: float float single currency interest rate swap
classes.label: float float single currency interest rate swap
classes.definition: interest rate swap that exchanges cashflows based on two different floating interest rates in the same currency

classes.name: floating interest rate leg
classes.label: floating interest rate leg
classes.definition: floating leg in which variable interest is paid on some notional amount, linked to some underlying interest reference rate

classes.name: inflation leg
classes.label: inflation leg
classes.definition: floating rate leg of an inflation swap linked to an inflation index, such as the Consumer Price Index (CPI)

classes.name: inflation swap
classes.label: inflation swap
classes.definition: rate swap in which one party pays an amount calculated using an inflation rate index, and the other party pays an amount calculated using another inflation rate index, or a fixed or floating interest rate

classes.name: interest rate swap
classes.label: interest rate swap
classes.definition: swap in which the reference (underlier) for at least one leg is an interest rate

classes.name: interest rate swap leg
classes.label: interest rate swap leg
classes.definition: swap leg that has an interest rate payment stream, including both a parametric and cashflow representation for the stream of payments

classes.name: notional step amount
classes.label: notional step amount
classes.definition: the amount of money that is subtracted from the notional on each step date

classes.name: notional step change event
classes.label: notional step change event
classes.definition: event in which a step change in the notional amount for a given swap leg occurs

classes.name: notional step period length
classes.label: notional step period length
classes.definition: recurrence interval indicating the frequency with which step changes occur, which is a multiple of the calculation period in the calculation schedule

classes.name: notional step schedule
classes.label: notional step schedule
classes.definition: schedule of changes in the notional amount on which interest is paid, comprising the regular sequence of step events

classes.name: overnight index swap
classes.label: overnight index swap
classes.definition: swap in which the periodic payments for one leg are based on an overnight interest rate index multiplied by the same notional amount upon which payments for the other leg of the swap are based

classes.name: overnight rate index leg
classes.label: overnight rate index leg
classes.definition: floating leg in which periodic payments are based on an overnight interest rate index multiplied by the same notional amount on which the payments for the other leg of the swap are based

classes.name: plain vanilla interest rate swap
classes.label: plain vanilla interest rate swap
classes.definition: fixed-float single currency interest rate swap in which interest payments are netted, the notional principal does not change, and there are no embedded options
parents: fixed float single currency interest rate swap

classes.name: single currency interest rate swap
classes.label: single currency interest rate swap
classes.definition: interest rate swap in which the two streams of interest payments are in the same currency

classes.name: zero coupon interest rate swap
classes.label: zero coupon interest rate swap
classes.definition: interest rate swap in which the fixed rate cash flows are compounded and paid once on the expiration date, rather than periodically; the payments on the other side (which can be based on a floating interest rate or a fixed rate) follow typical swap payment schedules

classes.name: dispersion swap index constituents leg
classes.label: dispersion swap index constituents leg
classes.definition: dispersion leg whose underlier is a defined set of constituents of a given equity index

classes.name: dispersion swap index leg
classes.label: dispersion swap index leg
classes.definition: dispersion leg whose underlier is an equity index

classes.name: dividend leg
classes.label: dividend leg
classes.definition: floating leg of a dividend swap

classes.name: dividend swap
classes.label: dividend swap
classes.definition: equity swap that has at least one leg whose underlier is a dividend stream

classes.name: equity correlation swap
classes.label: equity correlation swap
classes.definition: correlation swap that allows one to hedge risks associated with the observed average correlation of a collection of underlying equity products

classes.name: equity price return swap
classes.label: equity price return swap
classes.definition: return swap whose return leg underlier is based on equities

classes.name: equity return leg
classes.label: equity return leg
classes.definition: return leg whose income is based on equities

classes.name: equity swap
classes.label: equity swap
classes.definition: swap whose payments are linked to the change in value of underlying equities (e.g. shares, basket of equities or index) or their cashflow(s)

classes.name: equity total return swap
classes.label: equity total return swap
classes.definition: total return swap whose return leg underlier is based on equities

classes.name: equity variance swap
classes.label: equity variance swap
classes.definition: dispersion swap in which the parties agree to exchange payments based on the difference between (i) the realized variance of the price changes of a specified equity underlier over a stated observation period and (ii) a fixed amount of variance that is agreed when the contract is executed

classes.name: equity volatility swap
classes.label: equity volatility swap
classes.definition: dispersion swap that is a forward contract on the variability of movements in the price of its underlying equities

classes.name: qualifying dividend period
classes.label: qualifying dividend period
classes.definition: date period over which the sum of all qualifying dividends paid by the relevant issuers as identified in the swap terms is calculated

classes.name: special dividend leg terms
classes.label: special dividend leg terms
classes.definition: terms that are invoked if special dividend and memorial dividends are applicable

classes.name: basket of debt instruments
classes.label: basket of debt instruments
classes.definition: basket of securities whose constituents are debt instruments

classes.name: capitalized lease obligation debt basket
classes.label: capitalized lease obligation debt basket
classes.definition: basket of debt instruments whose constituents are contracts entitling a renter the temporary use of an asset and, in accounting terms, has asset ownership characteristics

classes.name: contribution debt basket
classes.label: contribution debt basket
classes.definition: basket of debt instruments that allows a company to incur an amount of indebtedness that is equal to (or in top tier sponsor transactions in the U.S., up to two times) the amount of equity contributed to the group

classes.name: credit facility debt basket
classes.label: credit facility debt basket
classes.definition: basket of securities whose constituents are credit agreements that allow the borrower to periodically take out money over an extended period of time rather than reapplying for a loan every time they need funds

classes.name: debt instrument derivative
classes.label: debt instrument derivative
classes.definition: security-based derivative whose underlier is a debt observable

classes.name: equity derivative
classes.label: equity derivative
classes.definition: security-based derivative whose underlier is based on equities (e.g. shares, basket of equities or index) or their cashflow(s)

classes.name: general debt basket
classes.label: general debt basket
classes.definition: basket of debt instruments that provides additional capacity for potential funding and does not require the proceeds to be used for any particular purpose

classes.name: incremental facility debt basket
classes.label: incremental facility debt basket
classes.definition: basket of credit facilities whose constituents are extensible, allowing companies to borrow an additional term loan or revolving credit facility (or increase the commitments applicable thereto) under the same credit agreement subject to certain parameters

classes.name: local lines of credit debt basket
classes.label: local lines of credit debt basket
classes.definition: basket of debt instruments that may be relevant for companies with international operations, often permitting debt to be incurred by a non-guarantor restricted subsidiary

classes.name: non-guarantor debt basket
classes.label: non-guarantor debt basket
classes.definition: basket of debt instruments that include a provision allowing certain subsidiaries within a corporate group, which are not part of the loan guarantee, to incur a specified amount of indebtedness

classes.name: ratio debt basket
classes.label: ratio debt basket
classes.definition: basket of debt instruments whose constituents are specified based on a leverage ratio based on total debt rather than only secured debt

classes.name: security-based derivative
classes.label: security-based derivative
classes.definition: derivative instrument whose underlier is based on a security, including collections of securities and indices based on securities

classes.name: bankruptcy
classes.label: bankruptcy
classes.definition: credit event involving a change in state or condition in which a party becomes insolvent

classes.name: credit event
classes.label: credit event
classes.definition: event signifying a sudden change in credit standing, such as bankruptcy or a violation of a bond indenture or loan agreement, that raises doubts about the party's ability to meet current or future obligations

classes.name: cross default provision
classes.label: cross default provision
classes.definition: contract provision that triggers a default under one contract if the borrower defaults on another related obligation

classes.name: default event
classes.label: default event
classes.definition: credit event representing a failure to meet a contractual obligation, such as failure to repay a debt including interest or principal on a loan or security

classes.name: distressed ratings downgrade
classes.label: distressed ratings downgrade
classes.definition: credit event triggered when the credit rating of an obligation is downgraded to a distressed debt level

classes.name: downgrade
classes.label: downgrade
classes.definition: credit event triggered when the credit rating of a party or obligation is lowered

classes.name: entity-specific credit event
classes.label: entity-specific credit event
classes.definition: credit event that applies to a given legal person

classes.name: failure to pay
classes.label: failure to pay
classes.definition: default event that is triggered following any applicable grace period in which a payment obligation is missed

classes.name: failure to pay interest
classes.label: failure to pay interest
classes.definition: default event that where either an expected interest payment is missed altogether or the amount paid is less than the required amount

classes.name: failure to pay principal
classes.label: failure to pay principal
classes.definition: default event that where either an expected principal payment is missed altogether or the amount paid is less than the required amount

classes.name: filing for bankruptcy
classes.label: filing for bankruptcy
classes.definition: credit event that involves a request to a court to be recognized as bankrupt

classes.name: hard credit event
classes.label: hard credit event
classes.definition: default event that is not repairable

classes.name: installment default
classes.label: installment default
classes.definition: default event involving non-payment of several installment payments as scheduled in the terms of the agreement, or non-payment of a call by the beneficial owner

classes.name: interest obligation in light of default
classes.label: interest obligation in light of default
classes.definition: obligation in respect of default(s) in the performance of any payment obligation

classes.name: maturity extension
classes.label: maturity extension
classes.definition: credit event involving extension of payments beyond the original maturity date of the obligation

classes.name: moratorium
classes.label: moratorium
classes.definition: entity-specific credit event involving a temporary suspension of payments until related issues are resolved

classes.name: obligation acceleration
classes.label: obligation acceleration
classes.definition: credit event triggered when one or more reference obligations become immediately due and payable as a result of a default or covenant breach on the reference entity's other debt instruments, subject to a materiality threshold

classes.name: obligation default
classes.label: obligation default
classes.definition: credit event triggered as a result of an obligation-specific default

classes.name: obligation restructuring
classes.label: obligation restructuring
classes.definition: credit event that materially impacts an obligation, such as an interest rate reduction, principal reduction, deferral of interest or principal, change in priority ranking, or change in currency or composition of payment

classes.name: obligation-specific credit event
classes.label: obligation-specific credit event
classes.definition: credit event that relates to an individual credit agreement or debt instrument (reference obligation)

classes.name: repudiation
classes.label: repudiation
classes.definition: credit event involving the refusal to honor the terms of a contract

classes.name: soft credit event
classes.label: soft credit event
classes.definition: default event that is repairable

classes.name: write-down
classes.label: write-down
classes.definition: obligation-specific credit event whereby the book value of the obligation, such as the outstanding principal amount, is reduced

classes.name: credit inquiry
classes.label: credit inquiry
classes.definition: request from a lender to a credit repository to obtain information regarding a prospective borrower's creditworthiness

classes.name: credit inquiry type
classes.label: credit inquiry type
classes.definition: classifier indicating whether a credit inquiry is a result of a borrower's direct authorization or by some indirect means

classes.name: credit message
classes.label: credit message
classes.definition: notice on a credit report to alert a reviewer of special or exceptional information

classes.name: credit message type
classes.label: credit message type
classes.definition: classifier that categorizes credit messages

classes.name: credit quality
classes.label: credit quality
classes.definition: classifier for borrowers, rates, or holdings in the lending market with respect to the quality of the credit

classes.name: credit rating
classes.label: credit rating
classes.definition: assessment of creditworthiness of a borrower generally or with respect to a particular debt or financial obligation

classes.name: credit rating agency
classes.label: credit rating agency
classes.definition: rating agency that publishes reports assessing the creditworthiness of a borrower or legal entity, either generally or with respect to a specific obligation

classes.name: credit rating model
classes.label: credit rating model
classes.definition: algorithm for computing a credit rating

classes.name: credit score model type
classes.label: credit score model type
classes.definition: a type corresonding to a family of credit scoring algorithms sharing common characteristics

classes.name: credit rating scale
classes.label: credit rating scale
classes.definition: rating scale for assigning a credit rating to individual, entity, or instrument, including defining a set of codes or numeric scores and indicating how an assessment that is assigned a score based on that scale means

classes.name: credit report
classes.label: credit report
classes.definition: report describing the creditworthiness and related credit attributes of a borrower

classes.name: credit report category
classes.label: credit report category
classes.definition: classifier for credit reports, often available from multiple vendors

classes.name: credit report product
classes.label: credit report product
classes.definition: branded credit report offered in the marketplace

classes.name: credit tradeline
classes.label: credit tradeline
classes.definition: report derived from the transaction history of a credit account

classes.name: instrument credit rating
classes.label: instrument credit rating
classes.definition: investment credit rating that provides an opinion of creditworthiness of an instrument, typically with some relationship to the creditworthiness of the issuer(s)

classes.name: investment credit rating
classes.label: investment credit rating
classes.definition: credit rating that provides an opinion of creditworthiness of an investment, including but not limited to an instrument or organization

classes.name: organization credit rating
classes.label: organization credit rating
classes.definition: credit rating that provides an opinion of creditworthiness of an organization

classes.name: short term credit rating
classes.label: short term credit rating
classes.definition: credit rating that provides an opinion of the probability of an individual or organization going into default within a year

classes.name: accrual
classes.label: accrual
classes.definition: the process of accumulating interest or other income that has been earned but not paid

classes.name: accrued interest
classes.label: accrued interest
classes.definition: amount of interest that has been incurred, as of a specific date, on a loan or other financial obligation but has not yet been paid out

classes.name: amortization
classes.label: amortization
classes.definition: the process of reduction of debt or other costs through periodic charges to assets or liabilities, such as through principal payments on mortgages

classes.name: amortization schedule
classes.label: amortization schedule
classes.definition: schedule of periodic payments (repayment installments) that specify changes in the balance of the debt over time

classes.name: borrower
classes.label: borrower
classes.definition: party to a credit agreement that is obligated to repay the amount borrowed (principal) with interest and other fees according to the terms of the instrument

classes.name: borrower identification scheme
classes.label: borrower identification scheme
classes.definition: system for allocating identifiers to borrowers

classes.name: borrower identifier
classes.label: borrower identifier
classes.definition: sequence of characters, capable of uniquely identifying a borrower

classes.name: borrowing capacity
classes.label: borrowing capacity
classes.definition: upper bound on the total amount of money that a lender believes a party has the ability to repay an obligation when due, as of some point in time

classes.name: capital lease
classes.label: capital lease
classes.definition: lease that must be reflected on an organization's balance sheet as an asset and as a corresponding liability

classes.name: collateral
classes.label: collateral
classes.definition: something pledged as security to ensure fulfillment of an obligation to another party, to lend money, extend credit, or provision securities

classes.name: collateral value as of date
classes.label: collateral value as of date
classes.definition: appraised value of the collateral for an obligation as of a given date

classes.name: committed credit facility
classes.label: committed credit facility
classes.definition: credit facility that is a confirmed source of financing for the borrower, as long as the borrower meets the conditions of the agreement

classes.name: committed sub-facility
classes.label: committed sub-facility
classes.definition: contractually committed portion of a credit facility that is available to the borrower and may be associated with some specific collateral

classes.name: credit agreement
classes.label: credit agreement
classes.definition: contractual agreement in which a debtor receives something of value and typically agrees to repay the creditor by some date in the future, in some form (e.g., cash, securities, etc.), generally with interest

classes.name: credit agreement repaid at maturity
classes.label: credit agreement repaid at maturity
classes.definition: credit agreement in which accrued interest may be periodically repaid or paid at maturity, but principal is paid at maturity

classes.name: credit agreement repaid periodically
classes.label: credit agreement repaid periodically
classes.definition: credit agreement in which the principal and accrued interest may be periodically repaid or exchanged

classes.name: credit enhancement agreement
classes.label: credit enhancement agreement
classes.definition: collateral agreement that governs the exchange of collateral between parties to mitigate counterparty credit risk

classes.name: credit enhancement beneficiary
classes.label: credit enhancement beneficiary
classes.definition: party that benefits from the collateral or guarantee established under the agreement, i.e., that is protected against counterparty credit risk because the collateral or guarantee serves as security for the obligation(s) owed to them

classes.name: credit facility
classes.label: credit facility
classes.definition: credit agreement that allows the borrower to periodically take out money over an extended period of time rather than reapplying for a loan every time they need funds

classes.name: creditor
classes.label: creditor
classes.definition: a party to whom an obligation, such as an amount of money, or good, or performance of some service exists

classes.name: day-count convention
classes.label: day-count convention
classes.definition: a business recurrence interval convention that is used to calculate the number of days in an interest payment, which applies to the amount of accrued interest or the present value for debt instruments

classes.name: debt
classes.label: debt
classes.definition: obligation to pay something, such as an amount of money, good, service, or instrument

classes.name: debt terms
classes.label: debt terms
classes.definition: contract terms that specify the formal rights and obligations of borrower and lender under a contract in which funds are lent from the one party to the other

classes.name: debtor
classes.label: debtor
classes.definition: a party that owes a debt or other obligation to another party

classes.name: explicit contract event schedule
classes.label: explicit contract event schedule
classes.definition: schedule of events, including but not limited to payment events, rate reset events and others that will occur over the lifetime of the credit agreement

classes.name: fixed interest rate
classes.label: fixed interest rate
classes.definition: interest rate that does not fluctuate over the lifetime of a loan or other debt instrument

classes.name: floating interest rate
classes.label: floating interest rate
classes.definition: variable interest rate that is based on a specific index or benchmark rate

classes.name: full amortization
classes.label: full amortization
classes.definition: amortization in which the very last payment (which, if the schedule was calculated correctly, should be equal to all others) pays off all remaining principal and interest on the loan

classes.name: interest
classes.label: interest
classes.definition: the cost of using credit, or another's money, expressed as a rate per period of time, payable by a debtor to a creditor in consideration of the credit extended to the debtor

classes.name: interest calculation
classes.label: interest calculation
classes.definition: event reflecting the calculation of interest

classes.name: interest calculation schedule
classes.label: interest calculation schedule
classes.definition: regular, contract-specific schedule including the dates on which interest is calculated

classes.name: interest payment
classes.label: interest payment
classes.definition: event reflecting the actual payment of interest

classes.name: interest payment schedule
classes.label: interest payment schedule
classes.definition: regular, contract-specific schedule including the dates on which interest is due to be paid

classes.name: interest payment terms
classes.label: interest payment terms
classes.definition: contract terms for payment of interest on a debt

classes.name: interest rate reset
classes.label: interest rate reset
classes.definition: event reflecting a potential adjustment to an interest rate, typically corresponding to a change in the underlying benchmark interest rate or index specified in the contract

classes.name: interest rate reset schedule
classes.label: interest rate reset schedule
classes.definition: regular, contract-specific schedule including the dates on which a rate reset, and corresponding actual rate, is recalculated

classes.name: interest rate setting event
classes.label: interest rate setting event
classes.definition: event on which an initial rate for a given contract is set, which may be relative the the occurrence of some other contract lifecycle event, such as the execution date

classes.name: lease
classes.label: lease
classes.definition: credit agreement permitting the use of real estate, equipment or another asset, such as a vehicle, by the owner of that asset (the lessor) to a user (the lessee) for a specific period of time in return for payment as specified in the agreement

classes.name: lender
classes.label: lender
classes.definition: a party that extends credit or money to a borrower with the expectation of being repaid, usually with interest

classes.name: managed interest rate
classes.label: managed interest rate
classes.definition: variable interest rate charged by a financial institution for borrowing that is not prescribed as a margin over base rate but is set from time to time by the institution

classes.name: motor vehicle lease
classes.label: motor vehicle lease
classes.definition: lease of a motor vehicle for a fixed period of time at an agreed amount of money

classes.name: negative amortization
classes.label: negative amortization
classes.definition: amortization in which the payments made do not cover the interest due

classes.name: non-physical collateral
classes.label: non-physical collateral
classes.definition: asset pledged as collateral that is a financial asset, rather than physical asset

classes.name: partial amortization
classes.label: partial amortization
classes.definition: amortization in which the very last payment the last payment due may be a large balloon payment of all remaining principal and interest

classes.name: physical collateral
classes.label: physical collateral
classes.definition: asset pledged as collateral that has a material form, i.e., is a physical asset of the obligor

classes.name: principal
classes.label: principal
classes.definition: with respect to a debt: the value of an obligation, such as a bond or loan, raised and that must be repaid at maturity; for investments: the original amount of money invested, separate from any associated interest, dividends or capital gains

classes.name: principal payment
classes.label: principal payment
classes.definition: event reflecting the actual payment of some amount of the principal of a debt

classes.name: principal payment schedule
classes.label: principal payment schedule
classes.definition: regular, contract-specific schedule including the dates on which some percentage or all of the principal is due to be (re)paid

classes.name: principal repayment terms
classes.label: principal repayment terms
classes.definition: contract terms that specify requirements for repayment of the principal

classes.name: projected contract event schedule
classes.label: projected contract event schedule
classes.definition: schedule of events, including but not limited to anticipated payment events, rate reset events and others that are expected to occur over the lifetime of the contract

classes.name: rate reset time of day
classes.label: rate reset time of day
classes.definition: time of day that an interest rate is reset, as indicated by some interest rate authority or market data provider

classes.name: retail credit facility
classes.label: retail credit facility
classes.definition: credit facility that is a loan or line of credit used by retailers and real estate companies

classes.name: revolving line of credit
classes.label: revolving line of credit
classes.definition: credit facility that enables the borrower to withdraw funds, repay, and withdraw again

classes.name: security agreement
classes.label: security agreement
classes.definition: collateral agreement that grants a financial interest in some collateral to a party that is not an owner of that collateral, specifying terms including relative duties and rights, over and above those specified in the primary contract, regarding the disposition of the asset used as collateral

classes.name: sub-facility
classes.label: sub-facility
classes.definition: portion of a credit facility extended to the borrower for some purpose, possibly per some schedule specified in the facility

classes.name: uncommitted credit facility
classes.label: uncommitted credit facility
classes.definition: credit facility that has yet to be confirmed as a source of financing for the borrower

classes.name: uncommitted sub-facility
classes.label: uncommitted sub-facility
classes.definition: sub-facility that has yet to be confirmed as a source of financing for the borrower

classes.name: variable interest rate
classes.label: variable interest rate
classes.definition: an interest rate that is allowed to vary over the maturity of a loan or other debt instrument

classes.name: collateralized guaranty
classes.label: collateralized guaranty
classes.definition: guaranty that takes the form of some asset that is pledged by a borrower to a lender (usually in return for a loan)

classes.name: government guaranty
classes.label: government guaranty
classes.definition: guaranty provided by a government entity, such as for a government-backed security

classes.name: guarantor
classes.label: guarantor
classes.definition: party that guarantees, endorses, or provides indemnity for some obligation on behalf of some other party

classes.name: guaranty
classes.label: guaranty
classes.definition: commitment whereby something is formally assured if a party with primary liability fails to perform

classes.name: insurance-backed guaranty
classes.label: insurance-backed guaranty
classes.definition: guaranty that is realized as an insurance policy

classes.name: insurance policy
classes.label: insurance policy
classes.definition: contract that (1) puts an indemnity cover into effect, (2) serves as a legal evidence of the insurance agreement, (3) sets out the exact terms on which the indemnity cover has been provided, and (4) states associated information such as the (a) specific risks and perils covered, (b) duration of coverage, (c) amount of premium, (d) mode of premium payment, and (e) deductibles, if any

classes.name: insurer
classes.label: insurer
classes.definition: financial service provider that issues an insurance policy

classes.name: joint guaranty
classes.label: joint guaranty
classes.definition: guaranty provided by at least two parties, jointly and severally

classes.name: letter of credit
classes.label: letter of credit
classes.definition: letter from a bank or other creditworthy institution guaranteeing that a buyer's payment to a seller will be received on time and for the correct amount

classes.name: letter of credit guaranty
classes.label: letter of credit guaranty
classes.definition: guaranty that takes the form of a letter of credit, i.e., a document issued by a bank guaranteeing the payment up to a stated amount for a specified period

classes.name: negative pledge
classes.label: negative pledge
classes.definition: guaranty whereby the issuer will not pledge any assets if doing so would result in less security for lender(s) or investor(s)

classes.name: policyholder
classes.label: policyholder
classes.definition: counterparty to and typically owner of an insurance policy

classes.name: priority level
classes.label: priority level
classes.definition: relative ranking that a guaranty has in the context of a contract, for example for a credit enhancement priority

classes.name: calculation agent
classes.label: calculation agent
classes.definition: party that is responsible for determining the value of an instrument and in some cases, determines how much the parties owe one another

classes.name: cash instrument
classes.label: cash instrument
classes.definition: financial instrument whose value is determined by the market and that is readily transferable (highly liquid)

classes.name: commodity instrument
classes.label: commodity instrument
classes.definition: financial instrument representing an ownership interest in bulk goods, such as raw materials and primary agricultural products

rules.property: has commodity value as of execution date

classes.name: currency instrument
classes.label: currency instrument
classes.definition: financial instrument used for the purposes of currency trading

classes.name: debt instrument
classes.label: debt instrument
classes.definition: financial instrument and credit agreement evidencing monies owed by the issuer to the holder on terms as specified

classes.name: derivative instrument
classes.label: derivative instrument
classes.definition: financial instrument that confers on its holders certain rights or obligations, whose value is derived from one or more underlying assets

classes.name: entitlement
classes.label: entitlement
classes.definition: financial instrument that provides the holder an interest in, or the privilege to subscribe to, or to receive specific assets under terms specified

classes.name: equity instrument
classes.label: equity instrument
classes.definition: financial instrument representing an ownership interest in an entity or pool of assets

classes.name: exempt security
classes.label: exempt security
classes.definition: security that is exempt from certain regulatory rules

classes.name: financial instrument
classes.label: financial instrument
classes.definition: written contract that gives rise to both a financial asset of one entity and a financial liability of another entity

classes.name: financial instrument identifier
classes.label: financial instrument identifier
classes.definition: sequence of characters uniquely identifying a financial instrument for some purpose and within a specified context

classes.name: future
classes.label: future
classes.definition: derivative instrument that obligates the buyer to receive and the seller to deliver the assets specified at an agreed price, at some later point in time

classes.name: issuer
classes.label: issuer
classes.definition: role of a party that issues (or proposes to issue in a formal filing) one or more financial instruments

classes.name: negotiable security
classes.label: negotiable security
classes.definition: security that can be transferred to another party

classes.name: non-negotiable security
classes.label: non-negotiable security
classes.definition: security that is not transferable to another party

classes.name: option
classes.label: option
classes.definition: derivative instrument that grants to the holder either the privilege to purchase or the privilege to sell the assets specified at a predetermined price or formula at or within a time period in the future

classes.name: packaged financial product

classes.definition: financial product that acts as a container for at least one financial instrument, including other financial products, and whose value is derived from, or based on a reference asset, market measure, or investment strategy

classes.name: promissory note
classes.label: promissory note
classes.definition: debt instrument that is a written promise by one party to another that commits that party to pay a specified sum on demand or within a specified time frame under specified terms

classes.name: redemption provision
classes.label: redemption provision
classes.definition: contract provision enabling the issuer (writer) to regain possession through repayment of some stipulated price

classes.name: securities transaction
classes.label: securities transaction
classes.definition: transaction between two or more parties involving the exchange of commonly defined financial products

classes.name: security
classes.label: security
classes.definition: financial instrument that can be bought or sold

classes.name: spot contract
classes.label: spot contract
classes.definition: financial instrument that settles for immediate delivery on a specified date

classes.name: standardized terms
classes.label: standardized terms
classes.definition: contract terms that, grouped together, that are generally and consistently reused across many contracts, published by some organization, and capable of being incorporated into a contract by reference

classes.name: underlier
classes.label: underlier

classes.name: adjusted closing price
classes.label: adjusted closing price
classes.definition: amended closing price to reflect a security's value after accounting for any corporate actions, such as stock splits, dividends, and rights offerings

classes.name: best bid
classes.label: best bid
classes.definition: highest bid price a prospective buyer is willing to pay at a particular time for a given security

classes.name: best offer
classes.label: best offer
classes.definition: lowest price acceptable to a prospective seller for a given security at a particular point in time

classes.name: bid ask spread
classes.label: bid ask spread
classes.definition: difference between an offer (ask) price and a bid price

classes.name: bid price
classes.label: bid price
classes.definition: price a prospective buyer is willing to pay

classes.name: clean price
classes.label: clean price
classes.definition: debt instrument price that does not include accrued interest

classes.name: closing price
classes.label: closing price
classes.definition: cash value of the last transacted price before the market closes

classes.name: closing price determination method
classes.label: closing price determination method
classes.definition: strategy for calculating or otherwise determining an official closing price

classes.name: collection of security prices
classes.label: collection of security prices
classes.definition: collection consisting of a series of prices, each of which has a specific date and time associated with it, for some security

classes.name: composite market
classes.label: composite market
classes.definition: group of exchanges and trading venues referenced for pricing purposes

classes.name: derived price
classes.label: derived price
classes.definition: price that stems from another source or calculation rather than being quoted or based on actual trading data

classes.name: dirty price

classes.name: high price
classes.label: high price
classes.definition: highest price for a given security over the period specified

classes.name: internal rate of return
